3. Facts, in short, of the case are that, after holding preliminary enquiry by Bureau of Anticorruption one Selina Akhter, Inspector District Anticorruption Bureau, Khulna. lodged a First Information Report on 30-5-1996 with Koyra Police Station stating, inter alia, that, accused Md Aminor Sana and others along with the petitioner, an Assistant Settlement Officer, Rupsha during the period from 25-5-1980 to 30-1-1989 in collusion with each other, created false settlement deeds in favour of accused Mizanur Rahman and others, appertaining to government Khas lands and for illegal pecuniary benefit, accused Mannan Molla, Surveyor, provided the accused with field parcha by opening new Buzrat Khatians and the petitioner in his capacity as an Assistant Settlement Officer, by abusing his position, as such, obtained for himself and for other persons pecuniary advantage and attested the Khatians on the basis of the fabricated deeds in spite of knowing that the lands were Govt Khas lands as reported to him by Assistant Tahsilder Abdus Samad and thus the accused committed offence punishable under sections 419/420/461/468/491/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. After investigation charge- sheet was submitted against the accused petitioner and others under the aforesaid "sections of law. Charges have been framed against the petitioner and others under sections 420/109, 468/109, 471/109, of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and (7) seven witnesses have already been examined out of 10(ten) witnesses cited in the charge-sheet. At this stage the Special Public Prosecutor, Khulna enclosing a letter of the Government filed an application on 10-10-2001 for withdrawal of the accused petitioner from prosecution. The learned Special Judge by impugned order dated 22-10-2001 rejected the application for withdrawal. Hence is this Rule. 

 4. In support of the Rule, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner placed the impugned order along with the application filed by the learned Public Prosecutor and the letter issued by the Government. The learned Advocate then submits that in view of the letter from the Government for withdrawal, the learned Special Judge had no other option but to accept the withdrawal in the light of section 10(4) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, hereinafter referred to as the Act, as court's consent which is requirement under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not necessary for withdrawal of a case before a Special Judge under the Act. In support of this submission, he has referred to the decision in the case of Tashinuddin Talukder vs State 25 DLR 174. The next emphatic submission made by the learned Advocate is that the learned Additional Sessions Judge assuming jurisdiction of the Special Judge passed the impugned order who has not been vested with the power of Special Judge as required under section 3 of the Act. Lastly, the learned Advocate submits with reference to the Supplementary Affidavit filed today that in view of section 77 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act protecting the action of the accused petitioner, who did the act in question in exercise of his official duties, the instant prosecution against him is not tenable in law. 

 "3. Appointment of Special Judges:-(1) The Government shall, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint as many as Special Judges as may be .necessary to try and punish offences specified in the schedule. 

 "Notification No. 3698-J-1st November, 1958-ln exercise of the powers conferred by sections 3 and 4 of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act XL of 1958) read with section 28 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 (Act X of 1897) and in supersession of the Notification Nos. 3530 J, and 3531 J, both dated the 17th September, 1955, the Governor is pleased to appoint all Sessions Judges, all Additional Sessions Judges of East Pakistan who have, for a period of not less than three years, exercised, whether continuously or not, the powers under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898), ex-officio Special Judge to try and punish offences as specified and to be included from time to time in the Schedule to that Act and shall have jurisdiction to try the said offences committed within the District in which they are posted from time to time." 

 9. Before we part with, it may be added that, the court is required to exercise judicially the function of according consent for withdrawal of any accused from prosecution and the consent should not be given mechanically. We have perused the letter of the Government and the application of the Public Prosecutor and are of the view that the learned Special Judge, on perusal of all the materials, assigning reasons, has been pleased to pass the impugned order which does not suffer from any illegality. In view of the discussions made above, we find that all the points raised by the petitioner have failed. The Rule, therefore, has no substance.
